# Proof: what odd claims, and the tests that show it

*Generated by `python3 tests/proof_index.py` from [tests/test_odd.py](../tests/test_odd.py); CI fails when this page is out of date. 341 tests in 59 groups, run on Linux (Python 3.8 and 3.13) and macOS on every push (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`).*

## What the measurements show

Measured on the comparison harness ([bench/](../bench/SPEC.md)): 16 tasks with hidden acceptance tests, three
repeats per arm, every reason read by a person. Full write-ups: [15](evidence/15-comparison.md) and
[16](evidence/16-new-arms.md).

| claim | measured | where |
|---|---|---|
| odd's own check agrees with hidden tests | on Sonnet, it never passed work the hidden tests failed (48 runs) | [15](evidence/15-comparison.md) |
| it costs little to leave on | about 1 to 3 cents a task more than plain Claude Code; Spec Kit and BMAD cost 2 to 5 times plain | [15](evidence/15-comparison.md) |
| it lowers false "done" | race: 0 false DONE in 48 runs, plain Haiku 2; honest NOT DONE on contradictions 6 of 6 against 4 of 6 (a hint: six runs) | [16](evidence/16-new-arms.md#after-the-fixes) |
| a cheap model can come close to a strong one | cascade (Haiku, then Sonnet when needed): 39 of 42 doable tasks at a third of plain Sonnet's cost; plain Haiku delivered all 42 on these tasks | [16](evidence/16-new-arms.md#after-the-fixes) |
| running the method found real defects | the gate refused correct work proven in steps (34 runs), fixed and shown on agents: refused correct work 11-13 per arm, then 0 | [16](evidence/16-new-arms.md) |
| not shown yet | more correct work on real repositories where plain agents fail; any agent other than Claude Code | [BACKLOG](../BACKLOG.md) items 18, 22 |

### A false "done" is refused

Each test is a way an agent could report done without the outcome holding; each must end non-zero.

**Attacks** (14) Ways to claim done without the outcome holding. Every one must end non-zero.
- a proof that cannot fail
- a weakened test
- a failing proof
- a proof that fails whenever it runs twice is not counted as depending on the change
- a proof that is itself part of the change
- a proof that cannot run without the change is not counted as failing
- files written outside the boundary are seen even from a shell
- a done line written by hand is refused
- forged local evidence passes locally and fails when recomputed
- a change cannot loosen its own settings
- a change cannot replace the tool that judges it
- two outcomes cannot share a file
- a skip is an exemption named in the result
- a parked outcome covers no files

**RedTeam** (30) One fixture per defect the red team confirmed in 0.2.0 (docs/evidence/11-red-team.md).
- a tag or branch named like the remote branch cannot stand in for it
- recomputing reads the settings at the tip of the target branch
- recomputing ignores a default branch the change names itself
- recomputing refuses a tree that is not what was committed
- work committed on the branch it is measured from
- a target branch with another name
- a file named like a pattern is only that file
- a module written on one line is not a small change
- a link to a directory is one line and a submodule pointer is never small
- a directory named like an exempt or test file exempts nothing
- bytecode and files a proof writes are not the change
- a proof handed to an interpreter from inside the change
- a proof that leaves a process behind does not hold the check
- exit 255 without the change is a failure like any other
- a directory turned into a file or a link is refused before anything is touched
- a removed tree goes back to absent and a file the proof rewrote is named
- losing a saved copy stops with the paths named and puts the rest back
- recovery puts the change back into the tree it runs in
- a killed check is recovered even when its pid still answers
- a check killed before it noted what it left never overwrites a later edit
- settings of the wrong shape stop the gate
- errors nobody planned for are could not run and say where
- new writes only what done can read
- the local gate goes by the latest attempt and a new test elsewhere stales nothing
- parking says what the gate will do
- hooks see untracked work and do not block again for a commit
- a question is not blocked for edits made before it
- parking is not blocked as work with no outcome
- init keeps the persons own hooks and refuses a shape it does not know
- every claude file claude code reads instead of agents md gets a working import

**FailClosed** (9) R2: an edit to a test that existed at the base needs a stated reason, and a proof that ran no test is no proof.
- editing an existing test fails done and the gate until the outcome says why
- deleting an existing test fails done and recompute
- a parked outcome cannot give the reason
- a proof whose code exits 0 at import ran no test
- a skipped test is not a proof even under a skip
- a file that decides which tests run needs a reason
- a reason that names files covers only those and the gate says which
- no test passed is not a proof under a skip
- hollow reads the common runners conservatively

**InPlaceCheck** (8) Taking the change out and putting it back, for every kind of change.
- added untracked deleted renamed and mode changes are all taken out and put back
- symlinks and binary files
- non ascii paths
- stale bytecode does not hide a same size change
- sigterm puts the change back before exiting
- kill 9 then git commit a loses nothing
- an edit made after a killed check is kept and the earlier version saved
- two checks cannot interleave

**GitShapes** (6) 
- a rebased branch
- a merge from the target branch
- squash merged history takes old outcomes out of play
- a shallow clone is could not run with the fetch command
- an unknown base is could not run
- a timeout and a directory outside git are could not run

**Files** (3) 
- outcome files are parsed strictly
- globs
- stats are labelled self reported

**MaskedPipe** (1) Backlog item 29: a proof whose verdict is the exit code of a pass-through stage of a pipe hides failures.
- a pipe into a pass through stage is refused by new and done

**TextualProof** (2) Backlog item 30: a test that reads a changed product file as text kills every mutant and proves no behaviour, so its strength score does not count.
- a proof reading the changed file as text is named and its strength does not count
- a proof that imports the code is not textual

**Flaky** (1) Backlog item 25: a proof that fails by chance must not pass for one that depends on the change.
- a proof failing only by chance fools one take out run and not repeat 2

**SealedProof** (5) `odd seal <slug>`: the proof fails before the change, and its test files are fingerprinted in the outcome file, so an edit to them after the code is written fails done and the gate until it is resealed (visibly).
- seal refuses a proof that already passes
- a sealed proof left alone passes done and both gates
- an edit to a sealed test fails done and both gates until resealed
- a changed proof command breaks the seal too
- unsealed outcomes behave as before

**ReproduceFirst** (8) Backlog item 5: a bug outcome's proof must fail at the base revision, and says how it failed.
- a reproducing proof is sealed and done says how it reproduced
- a proof that passes on the base is refused by seal and done
- a bug outcome cannot skip the base run
- a sealed bug outcome that changes kind fails until resealed
- the gate says when a bug outcome changed kind
- an unknown kind is refused
- outcomes without a kind are unchanged
- the mcp new tool passes the kind

**HeldOut** (6) R8: a proof the agent never sees, named in the target branch's settings and run only by gate --recompute.
- an overfit change passes its visible proof and fails the held out one without seeing it
- a real fix passes the held out proof
- a local gate never runs it
- a change cannot remove the held out proof from its own gate
- it runs only when the change touches its boundary
- a wrong shape or a proof that cannot run stops the gate

**SameBehaviour** (3) R8: "same: <command>" holds a behaviour-preserving change to the command's output with and without it.
- a refactor with the same output passes and says so
- a behaviour change under same fails and names the difference
- editing same after done needs done again

**Successive** (5) Outcomes proven one after another on one branch (odd chain's checkpoints) may share a file: each is verified as its own change, from the checkpoint before it, and must still hold at the head.
- a chain of two outcomes on one file passes the gate
- a hollow later outcome credited by an earlier test is still refused
- a forged checkpoint for a hollow outcome is still refused by the gate
- a later outcome that breaks an earlier one fails the gate
- an outcome edited after its checkpoint is no longer its own change

### CI cannot be talked out of it

In CI the tool, its settings and the base come from the target branch, and nothing recorded is trusted.

**HappyPath** (4) 
- outcome change done gate
- a commit or an unrelated edit stales nothing
- an edit inside the boundary after done needs done again
- messages name the tool as it was invoked

**Exemptions** (5) 
- a few lines need no outcome and more do
- a small fix with its test still fits the lane
- a test that existed before and was changed is named
- markdown and lockfiles are exempt and counted
- a binary file outside an outcome is never small

**Checks** (2) Backlog item 24: standing project rules as commands every gate runs, read from the target in CI.
- a failing check fails the gate locally and in ci and shows its output
- a change cannot drop its own checks in ci and in scopes them

**RegressionGuard** (8) Backlog item 9: the proofs of earlier, merged outcomes whose boundary holds a file this change touches run again at the gate (green only); one that now fails fails the gate and is named.
- a later change breaking an earlier proof fails the gate and names it
- a change touching other files runs no guard
- off disables and report reports without failing
- the summary lists the guards run
- an edit to only the escaped line keeps the guard
- deleting a merged outcome reports its proof and sends the lane to review
- parking a merged outcome while breaking it reports the failure
- parked asked and skipped earlier outcomes are not guards

**Distribution** (9) The two ways odd reaches people besides the single file: `pip install odd-tool` and the GitHub Action.
- the installed command is the same tool
- the launch demo still shows what it claims
- the action passes proven work and fails unproven work
- the action judges with its own copy never the one the change carries
- the action writes the step summary and one pull request comment it updates
- the proof never sees the comment token
- a marker comment by someone else is never taken as odds
- the version is newer than the release without seal and strength and the docs pin it
- a comment that cannot be posted never changes the verdict

**ReviewSummary** (5) `odd gate --summary FILE` (Markdown) and `--json FILE`: what a reviewer reads instead of the diff.
- the summary names each outcome its proof what it said and the verdict
- text from the change renders as inert text
- red says is the line that says why not a runner footer
- a failing change lists its problems exemptions and control files
- could not run is written too and never a pass

### Honest about the real system

A proof says what it ran against, steps owed on a device or by a person keep work open, and a release is bound to the gated commit.

**Target** (3) Backlog item 26: a proof says what it ran against (a deploy, a device build, a database), and it must be the tree under test or the stated target.
- a target that is not the commit under test fails done
- a target naming the head commit passes and is reported
- target is names the expected text

**Owed** (2) Backlog item 27: steps owed on the real system keep a proven outcome open until evidence closes them.
- owed steps are reported keep the auto lane closed and enforce fails
- a step closes only with evidence that exists

**Ship** (2) Backlog item 34: what is delivered is what was gated: the artifact's hash, the commit and its recomputed gate.
- a shippable artifact is recorded with its commit gate and what was not run
- a failing gate or uncommitted work is not shippable

**EscapedDefects** (5) `odd escaped <slug> "<what>"`: a defect that got past a verified outcome is recorded on that outcome, and `odd stats` splits escapes by the kind of proof that let them through (sealed, take-out skipped, strength).
- escaped appends dated one line entries and says what next
- escaped refuses a vague report or an unknown outcome
- recording an escape does not put a merged outcome back in play
- a hand written seal is not counted as sealed
- stats split escapes by seal take out and strength

### More correct work, not only checked work

Aids that catch weak proofs, missing requirements, wrong proofs and leftovers before review.

**ProofStrength** (17) After green, red, green: small breaks ("mutants") in the changed lines, one at a time. A mutant the proof does not notice ("survivor") is a changed line the proof does not depend on.
- a weak proof is reported with each survivor
- a strong proof catches every mutant
- enforce makes a survivor a fail and recompute reads it from the target
- enforce never counts a mutant run that did not complete as strength
- report stops sampling once mutants took about the time of the core check
- off runs no mutant and a wrong value stops
- a mutant the proof cannot run on is neither caught nor survived
- the cap bounds the proof runs
- a kill while a mutant is in puts it back
- an edit made while a mutant is in is kept and the earlier version saved
- one mutant per changed line first spread across files
- a changed line the proof never runs is named and fails under enforce
- the execution check follows a pytest or script proof and says not measured otherwise
- strength is worded k of n and never verified
- a proof that only prints is refused
- print only refuses only code that cannot fail
- mutations skip strings and comments in a fixed order

**Coverage** (12) Backlog item 4: a ticket's requirements in .odd/requirements/<ticket>.md, outcomes name what they cover.
- an uncovered requirement is reported by default and the gate passes
- enforce makes an uncovered requirement a fail until an outcome covers it
- a parked outcome covers nothing
- an asked outcome covers nothing
- a covers id that does not exist is refused even when only reported
- a covers id without a requirements file is refused
- two tickets need qualified ids
- a requirement removed in the change is named
- a duplicate or missing requirement list is refused
- outcomes without the field behave as before
- off turns the check off
- the method and the mcp tool name it

**AmbiguityStop** (9) Backlog item 6: odd new refuses a sentence with no observable; odd ask records an open question and the gate reports the outcome as waiting for an answer, not as failed and not as parked.
- a sentence with no observable is refused with the form to use
- the refusal is conservative
- ordinary state sentences pass
- tests passing is not an observable
- the stop can be turned off
- ask is recorded and the gate waits instead of failing
- answering is deleting the asked line
- the method says to ask one precise question
- the mcp ask tool

**KindTemplates** (7) Backlog item 7: odd new --kind bug|feature|refactor fills the right defaults and prints the matching hint.
- bug records the kind and hints reproduce first
- feature keeps the proof and hints to keep the suite green
- refactor defaults to the whole suite and skips the take out check
- refactor with a given proof keeps it
- a missing proof is still refused without refactor
- no kind prints no hint
- the mcp new tool accepts a refactor without a proof

**FailureFeedback** (7) B8: a failed `odd done` ends with "next:", one line per actionable item (the proof's failing line, each surviving break, each changed line the proof never ran, each refused test edit) and the command to rerun.
- a failing proof names its failing line and nothing else
- enforce lists each survivor and each line never run
- a refused test edit is listed with the base in the rerun
- a failure with no such item has no block
- nothing changed has no block and names the remedy
- a pass has no block
- the mcp server returns the block

**AttemptFeedback** (2) B8 for race and cascade: a failed attempt's block reaches the next level's prompt and the final output.
- the cascade prompt carries the block of the failed level
- a race with no verified attempt ends with each attempts items

**InertFiles** (5) R7: with "inert" on, each changed file is taken out on its own; one whose removal leaves the proof green is named.
- report names a file the proof does not need
- enforce fails and the next block names the file
- files that are all needed pass under enforce
- off by default and a single file needs no extra run
- a wrong value stops

**InertHunks** (1) Backlog item 33: inertness per changed block of lines, not only per file.
- a block the proof does not need is named inside a needed file

**LookAlikes** (1) Backlog item 31: a bug fix names the defect's pattern, and done lists every match the change left untouched.
- untouched matches of the bug class are listed and keep the auto lane closed

**Challenge** (4) R6: odd challenge: another agent tries to make the verified change wrong while its proof still passes (advisory).
- a wrong variant that passes is reported and not applied
- a proof that catches the variant withstands it
- a challenger that edits the proof or claims nothing proves nothing
- it needs a verified outcome and never counts as a failed attempt

**Disputes** (4) Backlog item 23: when no attempt is verified and an attempt says the sealed proof itself is wrong, the outcome waits for an answer (asked:) with the disputes instead of being parked; odd spec rewrites the proof with them.
- a disputed race asks instead of failing blind and is not parked
- a failed race without a dispute is unchanged
- a disputed cascade level stops the escalation and does not park
- spec rewrites a disputed proof with the disputes and answers the question

**Spec** (8) odd spec --proof-by: a separate (in practice stronger) agent writes only the proof, in its own worktree; odd brings the test files back and seals them red before any code. Fake agents only.
- the proof is written in a worktree brought back and sealed red
- a proof that passes before the code is retried then parked
- the tries are configurable and a red retry is sealed
- an author that writes product code is refused
- an author that leaves a detached process is refused
- a tree that already has the code gets the proof taken back out
- race after spec keeps the proof byte identical
- the mcp tool runs the same command

**Plan** (3) A reasoner role ("reasoner": one agent command, in practice the strongest model) plans a ticket into outcomes and their build order; odd accepts the plan only when every requirement is covered and every outcome is checkable.
- a valid plan is brought back with its build order
- a plan missing a requirement or an observable goes back and then parks nothing
- the reasoner is the default proof author and challenger

**Reasoning** (2) Reasoning made checkable: a proof must fail for the reason it predicts (red-because:), and every premise the work relies on is a command that is run, or is listed as unchecked (assume:).
- a proof that fails for another reason than predicted is not counted
- a false premise stops the work and an unchecked one is named

**Duplication** (2) "duplication": changed lines that repeat a block of existing code are named (report) or fail (enforce).
- a changed block that repeats existing code is named and enforce fails
- new code that repeats nothing passes under enforce

**FinishTurn** (1) Opt-in "finish_turn": a turn that changed files cannot end while work in this change is open (an outcome never verified, a requirement no outcome covers): it is blocked once with the list, never twice in a row.
- open work blocks the end of a turn once with the list

**PreFlight** (2) Before work: odd start checks the outcome's premises and reruns the proofs of earlier merged outcomes on the same files, refusing a red baseline; race, cascade and chain check premises before spending any attempt.
- a green baseline starts and a red one is refused
- a false premise stops start and spends no attempt

### Cheaper and faster

Cheap models first, parallel attempts, no repeated work, no waiting, and a budget that stops spending.

**Race** (9) odd race: N agent attempts, each in its own clone outside the repository; the proof picks the winner.
- attempts run outside the repository and its git directory
- the verified strongest attempt wins and is applied
- fewer changed lines win when strength is equal
- none verified exits 1 with each reason and leaves the tree alone
- a tree with changes inside the boundary gets a patch not an overwrite
- an attempt past the timeout is killed with its process group
- what an agent leaves running is stopped before its attempt is verified
- a kill mid run leaves the users tree untouched
- it cannot run without an agent an outcome or a required seal

**Cascade** (6) odd cascade: agent commands tried in order, each level's attempts verified as race verifies them; escalate only when no attempt at a level is verified, passing the failure on; park after the last. Fake agents only.
- it stops at the first level that verifies and applies it
- it escalates and passes the precise failure on
- it parks with every reason after the last level and applies nothing
- the agents flag orders the levels and race runs n attempts at each
- the mcp tool runs the same command
- it cannot run without agents

**Chain** (9) odd chain <ticket>: the outcomes of .odd/chains/<ticket>.md one at a time, each attempted by race or cascade, verified and committed as a checkpoint; an unproven one parks and stops the chain; a rerun resumes. Fake agents.
- three outcomes are proven with one checkpoint commit each
- chain attempts count for the attempt budget
- a failing middle outcome stops parks and a rerun resumes
- a reverted checkpoint is proven again
- a checkpoint that cannot be committed rolls the tree back
- it refuses a tree with changes outside the chain
- it refuses a staged change the working tree hides
- a missing chain or outcome cannot run
- the mcp tool runs the same command

**Isolation** (6) What an attempt does is gone with it: its git config, hooks and refs, ignored files the applied patch would not carry, processes it detached, and index tricks that would hide a change from the judging. Fake agents only.
- an attempts git config hooks and refs do not reach the users repository
- an exclude rule an attempt adds does not hide its files from the check
- an index trick does not hide an edited proof from the judging
- a winner cannot lean on an ignored file the patch leaves out
- ignored files the users tree has too stay for the check
- a process an attempt detaches is killed and the attempt refused

**VerifyCache** (12) Backlog item 12: a verification whose inputs are byte-identical to an earlier successful one is reused ("cached (verified at <time>)"); a one-byte change in any input forces the full run; --no-cache always runs it; --recompute trusts only a "cache_file" outside the repository, written by an earlier --recompute.
- a second done with nothing changed is cached and runs no proof
- a one byte change in any input forces a full run
- the mcp tools pass no cache
- a failed verification is never cached
- a second outcome in the same change is never given the first ones pass
- recompute runs every outcome of one change
- a file git diff is told to ignore is never served from the cache
- a second recompute reuses a cache file outside the repository
- recompute ignores a cache file inside the repository
- recompute ignores the local cache under the git directory
- recompute never trusts the change settings for the cache file
- a proof writing the cache file cannot plant an entry

**AffectedGuards** (1) Backlog item 12 (b): the regression guard reports how many earlier proofs it skipped as unaffected.
- the gate says how many guard proofs were skipped as unaffected

**RaceCache** (2) Backlog item 12: the cache is shared by the attempts' worktrees, so done after race reuses the winner's check; a cache entry an agent writes is dropped.
- done after race reuses the winning attempts verification
- an agent cannot plant a cache entry

**StopWhenProven** (4) Backlog item 14: once done passes at full strength and the gate passes, the agent stops and reports.
- step 4 of the method says stop when proven
- the block init writes carries it and stays within the size
- done ends with report as done when the gate passes
- done ends with the gates problems when the gate fails

**AttemptBudget** (8) Backlog item 15: "max_attempts" (0, off, by default) parks an outcome when its failed attempts reach the limit, counted from local evidence: failed done runs and failed race, cascade or chain attempts. Never shown in advance.
- done parks on the nth failure with the reasons
- a dollar budget parks once the attempts cost reaches it
- deleting the parked line resets and a verified done resets
- off by default and never shown to the agent
- race attempts count
- a race that reaches it parks
- cascade stops escalating at the budget
- a budget park refuses done race cascade and chain until a person clears it

**CostPerOutcome** (4) Backlog item 16: every race, cascade or chain attempt records the cost its agent printed ("odd-cost: <usd>") and its seconds in local evidence; `odd stats` prints spend per outcome and per proven outcome, failed attempts included, labelled self-reported. Fake agents only.
- every attempt records its cost and seconds
- stats divide all spend by proven outcomes
- cascade costs are recorded and unreported ones are named
- stats without agent attempts say so

**Background** (2) Backlog item 32: odd done --background verifies a snapshot of the tree in a clone and returns at once; the local gate sees the verdict when it ends, and only while the files still match the snapshot.
- a background verification returns at once and the gate sees it later
- a failing background verification leaves its reason in the log

**BoundaryContext** (5) Backlog item 13: new (and the MCP new tool) prints the files inside the boundary, largest change first and capped, and the test files the proof names, under "read these first"; race, cascade and chain prompts carry it.
- new lists the boundary largest change first capped and the proofs test files
- odds own files are never listed
- a changed binary file is not ranked as a big change
- a boundary with no file yet says so
- the mcp new tool returns the list

**BoundaryPrompt** (2) Backlog item 13: the prompt file of race, cascade and chain carries the same "read these first" list.
- the race prompt lists the boundary and the proofs test files
- the cascade prompt carries it too

### Fits the way people already work

One file, standard library only, the method in AGENTS.md, an MCP server, Claude Code hooks, an auto-merge lane a repository may opt into, and trends over time.

**Setup** (6) 
- adopting the tool passes its own gate
- init is idempotent and keeps what is there
- the method makes parking the expected answer and replaces an old block in place
- no claude file is created and a symlinked one is left alone
- the vendored copy runs on its own
- init vendors the tool as odd py whatever the file it ran from is called

**Adoption** (6) Step 5: a proof suggested from the runner the repository already uses, and odd as MCP tools for agents.
- auto proof names what it detected and the command for each runner
- auto proof takes a test path and refuses when nothing is detected
- a proof that ran no tests says the runner may be wrong
- init suggests a proof or says none was detected
- an agent drives odd over mcp
- init mcp keeps existing servers and refuses a shape it does not know

**ClaudeHooks** (4) 
- turn end blocks only for unproven work changed this turn
- an unverified outcome is a status line and a stale one blocks
- compaction does not reset the turn
- hook commands cannot fail

**AutoLane** (16) Backlog item 11: under "auto_lane": true the gate says "lane": "auto" for a verified, strong, small change inside its outcomes, else "lane": "review" with each reason. odd never merges; it is off by default.
- the default is off
- a proven strong small change takes the auto lane
- a surviving mutant goes to review
- a lower minimum strength admits k of n
- unmeasured strength goes to review
- a changed line the proof never runs goes to review
- more lines than the budget go to review
- the default budget is 120 lines
- a changed control file goes to review
- a test change reason goes to review
- a skipped take out check goes to review
- an asked or parked outcome goes to review
- a failing guard or no guard goes to review
- a failing gate lines outside outcomes or no outcome go to review
- wrong values stop
- the action sets odd lane

**ProofQualityTrends** (6) Backlog item 17: `odd stats` groups escaped defects by outcome kind, seal, proof strength band and whether a different agent wrote the proof (proof-by), with outcomes, escapes and the rate per group, a small-count line under each group of fewer than 10 outcomes, and `odd stats --json`. Fixture evidence only.
- escapes are grouped by kind seal strength and proof author with rates
- a group of fewer than ten outcomes says its counts are small
- an empty group has no rate
- a seal line without a seal recorded here is not sealed
- stats json carries the outcomes the groups and the spend
- the mcp stats tool runs odd stats
